cards.text: This is a Psalm of David, king of Israel (2 Samuel 5:3), written for the choirmaster. David is talking to the LORD, and he needs help. First words out of his mouth: “In You, O LORD, I have taken refuge”

cards.question: David asks God to save him by David's own righteousness.

cards.text: And David wants help NOW: “Incline Your ear to me; come quickly to my rescue.” Friend, I know that energy. That's me tapping the oven light eleven times like it'll make the batch bake FASTER.

cards.question: David reaches for a picture of the LORD keeping him safe. He tells Him, You are my ___ and my ___
David asks the LORD to lead him and guide him. For the sake of what?

cards.text: Then David pictures a trap. Somebody has laid out a net for him.

cards.question: There's a net laid out for David. Who does he say frees him from it?

cards.text: Then David says, “Into Your hands I commit my spirit;” Friend, I carry every cookie box in this bakery with my MUSTACHE, and I have dropped SO many, so David's smart to put his spirit in the LORD's hands and not in anybody's mustache.

cards.question: David puts his spirit into the LORD's hands. What does he say the LORD has already done for him?

cards.text: Hang on to that line. Centuries later, Jesus prays it from the cross, calling out to His Father right before He breathes His last (Luke 23:46).

cards.question: David says he trusts in the LORD and hates those who cling to worthless idols.

cards.text: And now David is glad. He says he'll rejoice in the LORD's loving devotion.

cards.question: David will rejoice because the LORD has seen his ___ and known the anguish of his soul

cards.text: The LORD hasn't handed David over to the enemy, and He's set David's feet in the open. Friend, after years in the back of a junk drawer, OPEN is my favorite word in this whole psalm.
Then the psalm takes a hard turn. David says, “Be merciful to me, O LORD, for I am in distress”

cards.question: David is in distress. What does he say his sorrow is doing to him?
Grief and groaning fill David's years. He says his own ___ has drained his strength

cards.text: And it's not just his enemies. David says he's a disgrace among them, and among his neighbors even more.

cards.question: When David's friends see him on the street, they hurry over to help him.

cards.text: Then David says, “I am forgotten like a dead man, out of mind.” Friend, I spent years under a pile of old receipts, so trust me, I know that neighborhood.

cards.question: David feels forgotten like a dead man. What else does he say he's like?

cards.text: And it gets worse. He hears the slander of many, and there's “terror on every side”

cards.question: David says the people conspiring against him are plotting to take his life.
David hears slander, and people are plotting against him. What does he tell the LORD right after that?

answers.text: That he trusts in the LORD
That he will fight them alone
That he will hide in the hills

cards.question: Back in verse 5, David put his spirit in the LORD's hands. Now what else does he say is in God's hands?

cards.text: Friend, my times used to sit in a junk drawer next to dead batteries swearing they still had a little charge, so David's got the better deal. And he asks the LORD to deliver him from his enemies and from those who pursue him.

cards.question: David asks the LORD to hide His face from His servant.

cards.text: David asks the LORD not to let him be ashamed, because he has called on Him. And he asks that the wicked be put to shame and lie silent in Sheol.

cards.question: David asks for lying lips to be silenced, lips that speak with ___ against the ___

cards.text: And now, from the same man who said he was like a broken vessel, this bursts out: “How great is Your goodness”

cards.question: David says God's goodness is laid up for those who ___ Him

cards.text: Laid up means stored away and waiting, like the backup batch I keep on the back rack for tired bakers. Friend, I have snacked on that backup batch so many times, I need a BACKUP for my backup.

cards.question: God hides those who take refuge in Him from the schemes of men. Where does He hide them?

answers.text: In the secret place of His presence
In a cave out in the hills
In the courts of the king

cards.question: David blesses the LORD for showing him loving devotion in a city at peace.

cards.text: Then David gets honest. In his alarm, he had said, “I am cut off from Your sight!” Friend, I know that one. In the back of a drawer, you're sure nobody is ever looking your way again.

cards.question: Even though David felt cut off from God's sight, God heard his plea for mercy when he called for help.

cards.text: Now David calls out to the LORD's people: “Love the LORD, all His saints.”

cards.question: David tells the saints that the LORD preserves the ___ but fully repays the ___
David's last words go to all who hope in the LORD. What does he tell them to be?

findings.problem: The card says Jesus "prays" the line from the cross. Luke 23:46 says Jesus "called out in a loud voice." The card relabels what the text says He did.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The joke (OPEN is my favorite word after years in the junk drawer) is a pleasant aside, not a real laugh. It is also one of four drawer jokes in the walkthrough (stop 1 card 14, stop 2 cards 6 and 12, stop 3 card 6).

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: Nothing on the earlier cards points toward sin. A baker who has only seen grief, groaning and distress would reasonably pick "labor" for what drained David's strength. "Iniquity" can only be reached by knowing the wording, not by reasoning about the meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The joke "my times used to sit in a junk drawer next to dead batteries" doesn't click. It puts the abstract "times" in a physical drawer, so the image is confused. The line "David's got the better deal" also sounds flip right after David asks to be saved from people plotting to kill him.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The card spends its words defining "laid up" (stored away and waiting). That is the dictionary pop-up's job.

rule.text: Don't spend card words explaining a hard word. Hard words get a dictionary pop-up (definitions.md, made after the cards).

findings.problem: The card tells no new part of the passage. It is only a word definition and a joke, and the second half of Psalm 31:19 (bestowed before the sons of men on those who take refuge in You) is never told. The joke also compares God's stored-up goodness to a backup batch that Papa Dorin keeps eating, which suggests that goodness runs out.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: "In the secret place of His presence" is the only answer in Bible phrasing and the only one about God. The other two ("In a cave out in the hills", "In the courts of the king") are plain, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
